hardiness.title: Hardiness Zone
hardiness.tooltip: Indicates cold tolerance according to USDA classification
hardiness.suitableIntro: This plant is suitable for the following USDA zones:

zoneDescriptions.0a: Extreme polar cold. Only extremely hardy plants survive.
zoneDescriptions.0b: Extreme polar cold. Only extremely hardy plants survive.
zoneDescriptions.1a: Arctic cold. Very few plants tolerate these temperatures.
zoneDescriptions.1b: Intense arctic cold. Requires ultra-hardy species.
zoneDescriptions.2a: Very severe winters. High mountain and tundra plants.
zoneDescriptions.2b: Very severe winters. Few ornamental species survive.
zoneDescriptions.3a: Harsh winters. Suitable for conifers and very hardy shrubs.
zoneDescriptions.3b: Harsh winters. Some hardy perennials thrive.
zoneDescriptions.4a: Cold winters. Compatible with many deciduous species.
zoneDescriptions.4b: Moderately cold winters. Good variety of fruit and ornamental trees.
zoneDescriptions.5a: Frequent winter frosts. Suitable for continental climates.
zoneDescriptions.5b: Regular frosts. Compatible with roses and ornamental shrubs.
zoneDescriptions.6a: Moderate frosts. Many Mediterranean plants with protection.
zoneDescriptions.6b: Occasional moderate frosts. Wide variety of crops.
zoneDescriptions.7a: Mild frosts. Suitable for inland Mediterranean climates.
zoneDescriptions.7b: Light frosts. Compatible with hardy citrus.
zoneDescriptions.8a: Mild winters. Ideal for Atlantic and Mediterranean climates.
zoneDescriptions.8b: Infrequent frosts. Suitable for hardy subtropicals.
zoneDescriptions.9a: Very rare frosts. Ideal for temperate coastal climates.
zoneDescriptions.9b: Occasional light frost possible. Suitable for mild coastal and subtropical climates.
zoneDescriptions.10a: Frost is rare. Ideal for warm subtropical and frost-free areas.
zoneDescriptions.10b: No significant frost. Warm subtropical climate.

returns.l3: Returns will be at the buyer's expense if the plants arrive in good condition and meet the measurements specified in the listing.
